edit.description: :377's widget `[[declaration.kind]]` row (inside `coverage_note_accepts_pre_parsed_locked_kinds`) is a `KindFactRow` — `common::kind_facts` builds it, `common::write_lock` writes it. :830's block is worse than hand-spelled: it is a top-level `[[kind]]` provenance array, not `[[declaration.kind]]`, carrying columns (`content = "file"`, `governs`) no `KindFactRow` has — measured this tick, `check` over that exact lock reports 15 kinds with no `custom-kind`, so `resolve_kind_units_runs_once_per_kind_not_twice` has no custom kind to resolve and its `.custom/member.toml` is governed by nobody. Write it through `common::write_lock` with a declaration that actually resolves, and pin the resolution (a `toml-document` kind needs a `named-field` identity — a markdown file kind is the cheaper spelling). :208, :285 and :690 stay hand-written: zero or arbitrary `emit_hash`/`import_hash` values no writer emits, plus a `layout_import` family `drift::Declarations` carries no field for.

:486's `[[declaration.nested_member]]` row (inside `an_embedded_kind_with_nested_members_renders_a_nonzero_embedded_marked_count`) is a `NestedMemberRow`, and the real writer renders that family (src/drift.rs:4493) — route it through `common::write_lock`, which writes no provenance row, so the skill on disk stays undeclared as the case requires. :292's corrupt lock stays hand-written.

summary: Route check_cost's and coverage_note's hand-spelled lock fixtures through `common::write_lock` — one of them declares a custom kind the engine never sees.

tests.asserts: `resolve_kind_units_runs_once_per_kind_not_twice` pins the custom kind's own resolution — the assertion names it, never a bare `resolves > 0` that 15 built-ins satisfy alone (engineering.md, "A green verdict is proven non-vacuous")
`coverage_note_accepts_pre_parsed_locked_kinds` still parses the widget kind out of the lock it was handed
the embedded-nested-members case still renders `supporting-doc (1 embedded)` and `skill (1: 0 declared, 1 undeclared)`

acceptance: cargo test green, with the custom-kind half of the resolve-count case now proven populated, and a `[[declaration.` grep over the two suites returning only the fixtures this entry names as writer-unproducible.
